what_worked: Strong thesis arc from power-law distribution through AI/geography/channel to audience-specific takeaways on slide 11.
fix_next: Use the assigned 1,000-row frozen dataset; every core statistic (8,782 startups, 5,025 zeros, 1,430 AI) appears drawn from a different source.
verdict: Compelling narrative built on the wrong dataset; accuracy collapses under verification.
factual_error_detail: S1-S3: Claims 8,782 startups vs assigned 1,000 rows. S3: 5,025 zero-MRR vs frozen 216 zero-revenue. S4: Top-10 = 42% vs frozen 49.6%. S5: Top-10 = 43.6% (contradicts own slide 4's 42%). S2: $15.4M monthly MRR vs frozen $15.6M total revenue (conflates MRR with total). S7: 1,430 AI startups vs frozen 197. S7: Median AI MRR $17 vs frozen median $503. S8: India 807 listings vs frozen 59 rows with country data for India. S10: 1,952 for-sale listings unverifiable against 1,000-row dataset.

evidence.insight: Slide 7 AI-as-noise framing and slide 9 mobile-floor vs web-lottery-ticket distinction show genuine analytical thinking; slide 11 audience-segmented takeaways add decision-usefulness beyond description.
evidence.narrative: Clear power-law thesis introduced slide 3, built through concentration (4-5), category (7), geography (8), channel (9), secondary market (10), synthesized in five truths (11). Purposeful and coherent sequence.
evidence.framing: No limitations slide, no mention of missingness (~24-29% across key fields), no acknowledgment that the analysis uses a 1,000-row sample. Deck presents itself as a full-census analysis of 8,782 startups without scoping caveats.
evidence.accuracy: Virtually every quantitative claim diverges from the frozen 1,000-row reference: row count (8,782 vs 1,000), zero-revenue (5,025 vs 216), top-10 share (42% vs 49.6%), AI count (1,430 vs 197), AI median ($17 vs $503). Slide 5 internally contradicts slide 4 (43.6% vs 42% for top 10). The deck appears to have used the full TrustMRR platform rather than the assigned dataset.
evidence.visual: Gamma template gives consistent typography and clean bar charts. AI-generated illustrations on every slide are decorative; slide 8 map has garbled/nonsensical country labels. No chart annotations, no source labels, no data tables.
evidence.ai_slop: AI-generated illustrations on every slide (whale, gold coins, futuristic office, price tags, garbled map). Consulting-speak ('disciplined capital wins,' 'picks-and-shovels') is borderline generic but not pervasive.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 3.5 to 3.0: slide 5 internally contradicts slide 4 on top-10 share (43.6% vs 42%), adding a ninth factual error; the deck's entire quantitative foundation is built on a dataset not matching the assignment. Other scores unchanged as preliminary reasoning was sound.
